title: Status Check Loop
description: Use WHILE loop with boolean flag to simulate system status checking.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "The navigation system is rebooting. We need to keep checking its status until it reports 'ready'. We'll use a boolean variable to track whether we're done."
story.context: Boolean flags are common in WHILE loops. You set a flag to False, then change it to True when the desired condition is met. This pattern is useful when the exit condition is complex or determined by external factors.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! You used a boolean flag to control the loop. This pattern is very common in real automation—keep checking until something changes."

instructions: Create variable ${checks} set to 0 (to count iterations)
After loop, log 'Navigation system ready after ${checks} checks'
hints: Boolean values must be strings: 'True' and 'False'
Nested IF inside WHILE needs proper indentation
Both IF and WHILE need END statements
solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Navigation System Check
    ${ready}=    Set Variable    False
    ${checks}=    Set Variable    0
    WHILE    '${ready}' == 'False'
        ${checks}=    Set Variable    ${checks + 1}
        Log    Check ${checks}: System not ready
        IF    ${checks} == 3
            ${ready}=    Set Variable    True
        END
    END
    Log    Navigation system ready after ${checks} checks

theory.title: Exercise 3.1.3: Boolean Flags in WHILE Loops
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Sometimes you don't know how many iterations you'll need. You just know you'll keep going until something specific happens. That's when boolean flags shine."

Boolean Flag Pattern

A boolean flag is a variable that tracks whether a condition has been met:

${done}=    Set Variable    False
WHILE    '${done}' == 'False'
    # Do work...
    IF    ${some_condition}
        ${done}=    Set Variable    True
    END
END

Why Use Flags?

  • Exit condition depends on complex logic
  • Multiple conditions might end the loop
  • Makes code more readable than complex expressions

⚠️ String vs Boolean

In Robot Framework, boolean values are typically strings:

  • Use: 'True' and 'False' (strings)
  • Or: ${True} and ${False} (built-in variables)
  • Comparison: '${var}' == 'True'
